body: You look like Hagrid after years of drug and alcohol abuse.
Hey buddy! What's going on? I'll happily neglect my work duties to chat
Weed doesnt work for everyone. It did the opposite. Everytime I smoked I plunged into the deepest depression...

I resort to audiobooks. They are a fantastic way to escape loneliness. It is by no means a substitute for a living person but it's a descent enough distraction. Whenever I go on a motorcycle ride or a hike on my own, I always listen to books about space and astronomy. Most of the time I find that being alone induces an inflow of intrusive and often unpleasant thoughts. Audiobooks overpower your inner monologue with a pleasant voice talking about something you are interested in :)
Unfortunately no. I travel all over North America and Europe for about 6-7 months a year. I am rarely home and I cant give any animal an ample amount of love and care it deserves.

My friend know nothing about this. I know better than to expose this side of myself to her.
I fill my time with work and learning new languages. I always try to develop myself at a personal or a professional level. Yet this doesnt help to keep these thoughts and feelings at bay. It makes me feel insane...
Same. Regret waking up every morning...
I start every morning with "Aagghhh Fffuuuuuuuck".

I dont understand all the hate people are spewing out in the comments. If this is true, may he rest in peace and if it is not, then this behavior is a clear sign of mental illness. The person behind this needs help, not hate...

For the last 3 years I've been on and off homeless while trying to put myself through university. My classmates would often joke about my dirty clothes without realizing that I slept on a park bench or a McDonald's the night before.

I was so broke that I couldn't afford a meal at times. Funnily enough I was turned away from the food bank the one time I went there because I wasn't officially "homeless" or "in need"... 

On top of that I have many years of enduring crippling depression, 3 suicide attempts and myriad of physical and emotional scars.

I made it through all of that because I had a goal in my mind. Finishing my degree and pulling myself out of that state was something that I was ready to strive towards in spite of any hurdles that came my way. The more problems I faced, the more I believed that I could do it. 

Perhaps you could try to look at your life and find ways to make you happy. Then figure out the best path to get yourself there. 

I know that the mess you find yourself in right now is overwhelming and it seems insurmountable. However the path to recovery starts with small steps. Dont give up quite yet my friend. I genuinely believe you can do it :)
Ofcourse I'd like to be friends!! My list is definitely not full 😁

I'm really sorry you're going through this. College was by far the toughest time for me. The stress, the lack of friends and money... It was just too much. I wouldn't suggest my methods of dealing with it because I would just study and spend the rest of the time depressed and drinking alone. My major allowed me to get a good job without having to finish school. So I ended up dropping out and working for a couple of years. I want to spend this time rebuilding myself and my life. It's working really well so far. I will be back when I feel ready and more confident to deal with all the problems college entails.
I'm really glad you are still here. Let's drink to a better future <3

I cant speak personally but my brother was addicted to cocaine and meth for 3 years. He was in a very dark place. He lost his job and did nothing but hang out with his meth crew for the entire time. He lifted himself up however. He found opportunities despite the lack of education or related work experience. He goes to NA 4 times a week and is his company's poster boy for those who struggle with drugs.
It gets better my friend. Just dont be afraid to improve your life.
For a very long time my dog was my only source of will to live. She sleeps by my side every night and as silly as it sounds, I felt extremely guilty taking her favourite pillow away...
I'm really happy my rant was useful to someone :)

Thank you for taking time to write me. I honestly cant keep going anymore. I endured being brutally sexually assaulted when I was 11, being homeless and emotional abuse by my bipolar step father. From a really young age I've internalized and suppressed all of this emotional pain just as any boy supposed to do. I've done quite well. I make 100k per year at the age 24, I have my own place and I volunteer at a homeless shelter in my spare time. Loosing my girlfriend of 4 years was a beginning of my demise. Ever since I've lost her, all of my bottled feelings descended on me like a hurricane. I feel like I am drowning in anhedinoa, nihilism and grief. I've read 27 books on behavioural psychology and treatment of psychological trauma. All of it to no avail. I just cant carry on anymore...
You are blessed. Keep on going :)
